critical_code_review_comments: v60.1.162 is exactly the kind of surgical patch I would recommend — remove the redundant defensive filter and rely on the canonical server-side source of truth (Firestore status='live'). Consider: if Firestore startDatum/eindDatum fields are sometimes plain JS Date / string / null, that's a data-quality issue worth fixing in the brand-autocomplete worker (normalize to Firestore Timestamp on write) so future filters can rely on the type. This is not blocking v60.1.162.

rca_of_the_issue: ROOT CAUSE: paintUitgelicht had a redundant client-side defensive filter `c.startDatum.toMillis() <= now && c.eindDatum.toMillis() >= now` AFTER the Firestore query already filtered `where('status','==','live')`. The .toMillis() call assumes Firestore Timestamp type. When campaigns were written with plain JS Date / ISO string / null (e.g. from older migration, manual Firestore console edit, or worker writing a non-Timestamp), the filter threw silently and the campaign was discarded — producing the 'Nog geen actieve partner-campagnes' empty state despite live: 1 in console. REPRODUCTION: Create campaign with status='live' and startDatum set to a JS Date (not firebase.firestore.Timestamp) — the campaign would be returned by the query but filtered out client-side. MITIGATION (v60.1.162): Removed the entire date-window post-filter. Source of truth is now the Firestore query + backend brand-autocomplete worker which transitions status='live' → 'completed' when eindDatum passes. Single line filter retained for the defensive null/undefined guard: `return c && c.status === 'live';`.
